feedback: Correct: the long-necked, four-legged one is Brachiosaurus (or Diplodocus) — the very long neck and small head are the giveaway; the two-legged one with the big head, sharp teeth and tiny arms is Tyrannosaurus rex.
If the child labels the long-necked one 'T. rex' too, contrast the features side by side — long neck versus tiny arms and big head — and re-match each name.
If they name without a reason, insist on the 'because': which feature tells you?
If they mis-assign a feature (e.g. thinks the back plates are wings, or that T. rex had big arms), re-anchor the species to its correct feature.
activities.intendedInsight: Naming rests on a visible feature, not a guess; the 'what feature helped you decide' step blocks pure name-guessing.
learnerActions: Answer 'Which one is Stegosaurus?' by choosing from pictures of the four.
Match each name to its described feature (e.g. 'three horns' → Triceratops).

Respond to the diagnostic prompt: shown a big four-legged dinosaur with a very long neck and small head (a shape cue), and a two-legged dinosaur with a huge head, sharp teeth and tiny arms, name each one AND say the feature that helped decide.
